title: The Hidden Cost of Task-Switching
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article explains business professor Sophie Leroy's concept of 'attention residue,' the mental cost of switching to a new task before finishing the previous one, which leaves people feeling sluggish and unfocused during transitions. It surveys common productivity strategies leaders use to reduce the number of transitions in a day, such as deep-work blocks, themed days, and task-batching. Its more distinctive recommendation is a transition ritual, a brief written note capturing a task's status and next step, which manufactures a sense of closure even when work is unfinished. The piece frames this ritual as complementary to the other strategies: while those reduce how many transitions occur, the ritual improves the quality of the transitions that remain.
points: People are especially vulnerable to distraction during transitions between tasks.
Sophie Leroy's research identifies 'attention residue' as the lingering mental cost of unfinished prior tasks.
Deep-work blocks, themed days, and task-batching are common strategies for reducing the number of transitions.
A transition ritual, a short written note on status and next steps, manufactures closure even on unfinished work.
Attention residue is heaviest when a task is left unfinished and open-ended, making the ritual especially useful.
